content:
Two years ago when Apple launched the M4 Mac mini, teardown reports immediately brought good news: the built-in SSD was not soldered to the logic board. Users could later upgrade the storage capacity themselves, and we even demonstrated how to do it.

However, the newly released M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini appear to have the storage chips re-soldered onto the logic board.

The NAND flash memory on the new Mac mini being soldered onto the logic board is a step backwards.

Expand Mac mini pointed out in a blog post that the NAND flash memory on the new machine is soldered directly onto the logic board, similar to the situation with the M1 and M2 Mac mini. In other words, the SSD module can no longer be removed.

Expand Mac mini has been selling storage upgrade modules for the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini. However, they said that as things stand, "support for the M6 and M5 Pro seems difficult to achieve".

No slot means nothing to swap, and there is almost no room left for us. Back in August we said we would expand coverage after testing the actual machines. This is the result, but it is not what we hoped to see. We will continue to look for a way out, but support for the M6 and M5 Pro seems unlikely to materialise. If the situation changes, you will be the first to know right here.

For comparison: Expand Mac mini's 1TB SSD expansion module for the M4 Mac mini is priced at US$300. Apple charges US$500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini's 2TB module sells for US$420, while Apple's equivalent upgrade costs US$1,000.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple's repair guide still indicates that the SSD is removable. We have not yet seen any teardown reports to confirm this.

If you are using an M4 Mac mini and want to upgrade the storage, you can try following the detailed tutorial written by 9to5Mac's Jeff Benjamin.

Although it is not a direct internal storage upgrade, Satechi has launched a clever accessory that combines an SSD enclosure with additional ports, designed specifically for the M6 Mac mini.
